einzeiler: Tressie McMillan Cottom joins a live audience to explore the history of Black Loyalists.
kurzfassung: Host Nicole Hill and guest Tressie McMillan Cottom perform a live show exploring the history of Black Loyalists during the American Revolution. Through interactive audience decisions, they trace how thousands of enslaved people fought for the British in exchange for freedom and relocated to Nova Scotia. The discussion highlights the complex choices ancestors faced, drawing parallels between historical struggles and modern experiences.
stichpunkte: Tressie McMillan Cottom joins Nicole Hill live on stage to discuss the dramatic history of Black Loyalists.
The narrative follows ancestors like David George who escaped slavery and sought freedom through the British.
Audience members participate using decision boards to vote on critical historical turning points.
Many enslaved people chose to side with the British due to the promise of freedom and better provisions.
The British evacuation of New York led thousands of Black Loyalists to settle in Nova Scotia.
Life in Nova Scotia brought severe hardship, leading to early race riots in Shelburne.
Communities like Birchtown provided refuge and became strong centers for free Black settlers.
Later expeditions led many settlers to establish a new community in Sierra Leone.

kapitel.titel: The American Revolution and the Choice of Sides
David George and Silver Bluff Baptist Church
Evacuation to Nova Scotia and the Book of Negroes
The Voyage to Sierra Leone and Final Reflections

clips.hook: Tracing generations back through oral history in North Carolina
clips.text: The guest explains that despite a lack of early written records, her family has preserved oral history going back seven generations in the same region.

clips.hook: Audience voting reveals an unexpected preference for the American side
clips.text: The host notes that this particular live audience is the first across multiple cities to choose the American patriots over the British.

clips.hook: Surviving bureaucracy only to be called stout in historical ledgers
clips.text: The speaker humorously reacts to the disrespectful descriptors used in official historical documents despite all the hardships survivors endured.

clips.hook: Naming Blacktown and reflecting on community agency
clips.text: The participants discuss whether their ancestors named their settlement themselves, emphasizing their autonomy in defining their spaces.

clips.hook: The intertwined existence of America and Black identity
clips.text: The guest argues that Black identity in America was forged as a direct response to the nation's foundational contradictions regarding freedom.

beschreibung:
Thousands of our ancestors escaped slavery during the American Revolution, fought for the British on the promise of freedom, and left an outsized legacy in the US, Canada, and beyond. Starring writer, sociologist, and MacArthur Fellow Tressie McMillian Cottom taped live on Juneteenth at the Institute for Contemporary Art at VCU in Richmond, VA.
